old.text: Existing benchmarks examine complementary aspects of scientific work, including ideation, goal-directed discovery, analytical decisions, and executable tasks ( Mo et al., 2026 ; Majumder et al., 2024 ; Gu et al., 2025 ; Chen et al., 2024 ) . OEB further evaluates evidence use, experimentation, and research-process integrity ( Shi et al., 2026 ) . DFM-Bench makes hypotheses, revisions, development paths, research runs, and contribution families explicit assessment objects. Table 1 compares their evaluation coverage; the accompanying definitions and qualifications appear in Appendix D.6 .

old.text: We evaluate DiscoveryRSI across four life-science domains: clinical and population health, therapeutic target prioritization, disease mechanisms, and population multi-omics. Inputs include the HCC clinical cohort, MIMIC-IV ( Johnson et al., 2023 ) , eICU ( Pollard et al., 2018 ) , UK Biobank ( Sudlow et al., 2015 ) , and molecular studies from GEO and ArrayExpress ( Edgar et al., 2002 ; Sarkans et al., 2021 ) . Agents inspect data and literature, formulate hypotheses, and develop investigation plans specifying comparisons, measurements, and interpretation criteria ( Figure 4 ).

To test transfer beyond life science, we add a battery setting with four domains: electrical diagnostics, health prediction, degradation mechanisms, and usage history and aging. The evidence pack covers capacity and impedance aging measurements ( Luh and Blank, 2024 ) , impedance-based health prediction ( Zhang et al., 2020 ; Jones et al., 2022 ) , degradation-mode analysis ( Li et al., 2025 ; Kirkaldy et al., 2024 ) , and path-dependent aging experiments ( Raj et al., 2020 ) . Investigations separate measured quantities from fitted degradation labels and specify cell, condition, and protocol splits. The same Lead–Generation–Evolution–Critique–Compiler loop is used, with battery-specific checks for operating conditions, sensing, physical plausibility, and competing explanations.

We perform full-parameter fine-tuning of DiscoveryRSI-27B with a 256K-token context window using hypothesis-credit-weighted supervision. From 15,792 collected research trajectories, attribution, filtering, and tokenization yield 2,397 training trajectories: 634 Lead, 861 Generation, and 902 Evolution histories. The training sequences contain 291.12 million tokens, of which 6.18 million (2.12%) receive direct supervision. We train for one epoch using Adam with a learning rate of 5 × 10 − 6 5\times 10^{-6} , a global batch size of 16, and BF16 precision. Detailed trajectory accounting, credit allocation, and token masking appear in Appendix C .

old.text: The battery applies the five-level DFM-Bench evaluation to 200 episodes and 351 generated hypotheses, with three AI reviews per hypothesis. The current panel reports a mean hypothesis quality of 5.61 on 165 complete scores, substantive progress on 214 of 366 transitions (58.47%), a mean complete-trajectory score of 81.52 across 152 paths, and a research round score of 71.25. 20 contribution families were identified, with 7 carrying diagnostic or research evidence.

Absolute quality ratings show a mixed profile. DiscoveryRSI-27B scores higher than GPT-6 Luna on importance (3.10 versus 2.94) and plausible, evidence-bounded claims (3.37 versus 3.16). Both receive 2.31 for advance over known work, while GPT-6 Luna scores higher on data fit, alternative explanations, and informative results. old.text: Discovery agents increasingly support hypothesis generation, experimental planning, and computational investigation. Co-Scientist develops hypotheses through multi-agent refinement ( Gottweis et al., 2026 ) , AI Scientist-v2 connects research ideation with agentic experimental search ( Yamada et al., 2025 ) , and Biomni integrates biomedical tools and data ( Huang et al., 2025 ) . Discovery Foundation Models frame problem formation and evidence-grounded revision as learnable capabilities ( Yang et al., 2026b ) , while ScienceIDE constructs environments for learning from scientific workflows ( Geng et al., 2026 ) . Evaluation spans scientific ideation in AgentIdeaBench ( Mo et al., 2026 ) , data-driven discovery in DiscoveryBench and BLADE ( Majumder et al., 2024 ; Gu et al., 2025 ) , executable investigations in ScienceAgentBench ( Chen et al., 2024 ) , and research-process assessment in OEB ( Shi et al., 2026 ) . DiscoveryRSI connects hypothesis development to subsequent model learning, while DFM-Bench makes hypotheses, revisions, development paths, research runs, and contribution families explicit evaluation objects.

Reward-guided training provides a foundation for converting generated experience into model updates. RAFT selects highly rated samples for fine-tuning ( Dong et al., 2023 ) , ReST-EM alternates generation and feedback-based filtering ( Singh et al., 2023 ) , and advantage-weighted regression learns through weighted likelihood objectives ( Peng et al., 2019 ) . SimpleTES further studies learning from scientific exploration trajectories ( Ye et al., 2026 ) . These approaches motivate the use of assessed research histories as supervision. DiscoveryRSI addresses the attribution problem within multi-agent hypothesis development: an assessment concerns a scientific proposal, whereas learning targets belong to the histories that contributed to it. Hypothesis credit optimization links these levels through documented contributions, bounded credit allocation, and supervision restricted to supported assistant actions.

Reflexion, GEPA, and ACE retain experience through verbal memory, prompt evolution, and contextual playbooks ( Shinn et al., 2023 ; Agrawal et al., 2025 ; Zhang et al., 2025b ) ; harness optimization extends adaptation to agent workflows and implementations ( Zhang et al., 2026a ; Lin et al., 2026 ) . Darwin Gödel Machine and Hyperagents study persistent program-level improvement ( Zhang et al., 2025a ; Zhang et al., 2026b ) , while MASS couples multi-agent workflow optimization with learning from selected executions ( Lee et al., 2026 ) . ScienceBuddy connects harness refinement with model learning ( Xue et al., 2026 ) , and RSI-Anything uses predictive world models to guide interaction and retained system updates ( Cui et al., 2026 ) . DiscoveryRSI brings these directions to hypothesis-centered research: evolving claims, evidence, and investigation decisions provide a shared record for contribution-based model learning, harness replay, and subsequent rediscovery. Its focus is how experience accumulated while developing scientific questions can improve later investigations.

DiscoveryRSI connects hypothesis development with learning from documented research contributions. The present work reaches concrete hypotheses and compiled investigation plans. The next step is to determine which proposals merit investigation, using solvers and frameworks such as RSI-Anything ( Cui et al., 2026 ) to execute, assess, and refine them. Closing the discovery loop further requires wet-lab validation and methods that turn supportive, negative, and inconclusive outcomes into improved research decisions. Extending hypothesis discovery and DFM-Bench to additional scientific domains will help establish how these capabilities generalize. Together, these directions advance the DFM vision ( Yang et al., 2026b ) of agents that formulate worthwhile questions, investigate them, and learn from the resulting evidence.

old.text: Weights and normalization factors are frozen before optimization. Domain balancing assigns 90% of the objective weight to life-science trajectories and 10% to battery-research trajectories. The objective uses offline weighted supervision; it does not involve online policy optimization.

new.text: Weights and normalization factors are frozen before optimization. The objective uses offline weighted supervision; it does not involve online policy optimization.

old.text: AgentIdeaBench scores final ideas with literature-verified critics; its grounding assessment is partial evidence-use coverage. Its generation-time refinement experiments do not constitute an explicit revision or ancestry-path evaluation object ( Mo et al., 2026 ) . DiscoveryBench evaluates reference-aligned hypotheses and analytical facets for supplied discovery goals; this provides partial hypothesis-merit and evidence-use coverage, rather than an open-ended merit or contribution-maturity rubric ( Majumder et al., 2024 ) . BLADE compares conceptual variables, transformations, and statistical models against expert analyses, providing partial evidence-use coverage through analytical decisions ( Gu et al., 2025 ) . ScienceAgentBench assesses generated programs, outputs, and task-stage rubrics; this is partial evidence-use coverage rather than evaluation of evolving scientific claims ( Chen et al., 2024 ) .
